messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital Course Summary:
The patient, a 76-year-old Caucasian male with a family history of Parkinson's disease, was admitted to our hospital after experiencing a shuffling gait. Neurological examination revealed bilateral rigidity and slow gait with reduced arm swing, as well as processing speed and memory difficulties. The patient also presented with urinary retention, orthostatic hypotension, erectile dysfunction, and stridor. Carbidopa/levodopa was unsuccessfully administered. The patient was diagnosed with multiple system atrophy (MSA), due to levodopa-unresponsive parkinsonism and autonomic dysfunction.

During the hospital course, the patient received comprehensive care from a multidisciplinary team, including neurologists and primary care physicians. Management of orthostatic hypotension and urinary retention were coordinated with the urology department. The patient was administered supportive therapy, including physical therapy and occupational therapy, to address mobility and activities of daily living. The patient's condition remained stable throughout his hospital stay.

At the time of discharge, the patient was instructed to continue with his current medications and follow up with his primary care physician and neurologist. The patient was also instructed to contact his healthcare provider if any new or worsening symptoms arise.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Follow-up Instructions:
1. Continue current medication regimen as prescribed.
2. Follow up with primary care physician and neurologist.
3. Contact healthcare provider if any new or worsening symptoms arise.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
The condition chiefly responsible for the admission is multiple system atrophy, diagnosed from levodopa-unresponsive parkinsonism with autonomic dysfunction. In ICD-10-AM it is classified to chapter G (diseases of the nervous system), under G90.3 (multi-system degeneration). The category is therefore G90.

CODE: G90
